Add --use-fake-dmserver switch for Chromium builds

Testing local policies against fake_dmserver on Chromium previously
required passing both --enable-chrome-browser-cloud-management and
an explicit --device-management-url switch.

to default the device management server URL to the fake server port
and enable cloud management automatically.

Ignore OpenURL requests without a frame tree id during prerendering

Navigator::RequestOpenURL() needs a frame_tree_node_id to route requests
from prerendering frames to the correct frame tree. Replace the DCHECK
with an early return when that id is missing.

A synthetic click in a prerendering page can reach this path, so ignore
the request without terminating the renderer. Keep support for these
requests as separate work.

Add a regression test in PrerenderBrowserTest to check that the request
starts no navigation and that the prerendered page remains live and can
still be activated.

Browser test not run locally; no configured build output is available.

[AppRating] Support AppStoreRatingEnabled enterprise policy on Android

The AppStoreRatingEnabled policy is currently only configured for iOS.
This CL extends support for the policy to Android so that enterprise
administrators can disable the Google Play In-App Review prompt on
managed devices.

Specifically:
- Adds Android support to AppStoreRatingEnabled.yaml.
- Declares and registers prefs::kAppRatingPolicyEnabled.
- Maps policy::key::kAppStoreRatingEnabled to
  prefs::kAppRatingPolicyEnabled on Android.
- Guards AppRatingPromoController.maybeShowPromo() against the policy
  pref.
- Adds test coverage for the disabled policy state in
  AppRatingPromoControllerTest and policy pref mapping test data.

mojo: Skip redundant Stylize passes on Module

Module.Stylize() recursively calls Stylize() on each entry in
self.imports. Because transitive imports form a DAG of shared Module
instances within a loaded .mojom-module, shared dependency modules (such
as url.mojom, time.mojom, and geometry.mojom) underwent redundant
Stylize traversals hundreds of times per module.

Cache _stylizer_type on Module and skip subsequent Stylize() calls if
the module has already been stylized with the same stylizer type.

For //content/common:mojo_bindings__generator on a single core
(taskset -c 0), this reduces median wall time from 3.32s to 2.55s
(-0.77s, -23.1%).

Revert "Add --ignore-global-synthetics to CustomD8"

This reverts commit 25818ddfd2459c642dc31eb03bfad2fdc31b421d.

Reason for revert: D8 is gaining a native --ignore-globals flag
(https://r8-review.googlesource.com/c/r8/+/140140), so the CustomD8
flag is not needed. The follow-up (https://crrev.com/c/8527208) will
use the upstream flag once r8 rolls.

Original change's description:
> Add --ignore-global-synthetics to CustomD8
>
> Desugaring Java records in --intermediate mode makes D8 emit a "global
> synthetic" (RecordTag) and fail with "Attempt to create a global
> synthetic for 'Record desugaring' without a global-synthetics consumer"
> unless a consumer is registered. The flag installs a no-op consumer,
> the same thing AGP does for debug builds
> (useUniversalGlobalSyntheticsDex); a follow-up CL passes it from dex.py
> and adds a single dex with all global synthetics to debug APKs.
>
> Bug: 570626552

[iOS][Actor] Extract PostedObserverList from ActorTask

Extracts `ActorTask`'s posted observer registration and notification
logic into `PostedObserverList`, a generic Objective-C class wrapping
`CRBProtocolObservers`, for reuse by `ActorService`. Owners declare it
typed by their observer protocol, e.g.
`PostedObserverList<id<ActorTaskUpdatesObserver>>*`, so notification
blocks receive the observers typed as that protocol.

Delivery is now tracked per registration (`-addObserver:` to
`-removeObserver:`): removing and re-adding an observer before its
first registration runs drops the stale snapshot and queued
notifications, and duplicate `-addObserver:` calls are ignored.

[Android] Send drag end to a web drag source removed mid-drag

Make sure the web contents a drag started from always gets
ACTION_DRAG_ENDED.
-Previously, if the source tab's ContentView was removed from the view
 hierarchy during the drag (e.g. the user switched tabs, or a drop
 selected another tab), Android never sent it ACTION_DRAG_ENDED. The
 renderer then stayed in drag mode and the tab ignored input.
-Now, CompositorViewHolder remembers the current ContentView on
 ACTION_DRAG_STARTED if the drag came from it. On ACTION_DRAG_ENDED,
 if that ContentView's WebContents still reports a started drag via
 its DragStateTracker (which resets once the view handles the event),
 the event is delivered to the ContentView's drag listeners and
 onDragEvent directly. ContentView#dispatchDragEvent can't be used,
 since ViewGroup drops ACTION_DRAG_ENDED for a view that was detached
 mid-drag.

[composebox] Clear match selection when shift-tabbing out of dropdown

When keyboard-navigating into dropdown suggestions and pressing
shift-tab on the first visible match to move focus backward out of the
dropdown, `selectedMatchIndex` previously remained unchanged. Because
matches style `[selected]` with a focus indicator, the first match kept
its focus indicator while the newly focused element also displayed its
focus ring.

Updates `unselectOnTabExit()` and `willTabExitMatch()` to symmetrically
handle backward shift-tab navigation:

1. Add `getFirstVisibleIndex()` (and `getLastVisibleIndex()`) on
`ComposeboxDropdownElement`, accounting for hidden verbatim matches in
typed suggest.

2. Unselect the active match in `unselectOnTabExit()` when pressing
Shift-Tab on the first visible match will exit the match.

Reland "[composebox] Refactor dropdown Tab-exit unselection logic"

This is a reland of commit 6409248427854452004875dd939a0332deacca39

Updates the newly added test in `composebox_autocomplete_test.ts` to use
`createAutocompleteMatch()` instead of `as AutocompleteMatch`, as a
concurrent CL on main removed the `AutocompleteMatch` type import from
that test file.

Original change's description:
> [composebox] Refactor dropdown Tab-exit unselection logic
>
> Moves the logic for unselecting the active dropdown match when pressing
> Tab past the last visible match out of `ComposeboxEmbedderMixin` and
> into `ComposeboxDropdownElement` and `ComposeboxMatchElement`:
>
> 1. Add `omnibox::kComposeboxUnselectMatchOnTabExit` (disabled by
> default) in `composebox_features` and expose
> `composeboxUnselectMatchOnTabExit` via
> `SearchboxHandler::GetWebUIDataSourceDict`.
>
> 2. Add `ComposeboxMatchElement.willTabExitMatch()` to encapsulate
> whether pressing forward Tab will move focus outside the match rather
> than to an internal control (such as the remove button).
>
> 3. Add `ComposeboxDropdownElement.unselectOnTabExit()` to check whether
> the active match is the last visible match and will exit on Tab,
> allowing `getMaxVisibleIndex_()` to stay `protected`.
>
> 4. Gate `unselectOnTabExit()` behind `this.unselectMatchOnTabExit` in
> `ComposeboxEmbedderMixin.handleTab_()`, falling back to the existing
> inline logic when the flag is disabled.
>
> 5. Add unit tests in `searchbox_handler_unittest.cc`,
> `composebox_autocomplete_test.ts`, `composebox_dropdown_test.ts`, and
> `composebox_match_test.ts`.
>
> This is a pure refactoring with no intended behavior change.
>

[iOS][Actor] Hold Gemini confirmation yields until the user answers

`GeminiActuationHandler` answered a `kConfirmation` yield with `kOk`
without communicating with the actor task. It now interrupts the task
with the yield's message and holds the SDK callback until the user
accepts, the task stops, or the handler disconnects.

This change covers the happy path only; crbug.com/567035024 will be
the full implementation.

[base] Dynamically synchronize C++ and Rust logging level

This CL synchronizes the C++ and Rust logging levels, in order to avoid
wastefully passes log events from Rust to C++ that we already know we
want to discard.

* Maps C++ log severity to log::LevelFilter and updates
  log::set_max_level dynamically when SetMinLogLevel is called.

* Implements RustLogger::enabled using an atomic min log level check to
  avoid formatting arguments when logging is disabled.

* Uses a stack-allocated buffer for log file names in RustLogger::log
  to eliminate heap allocations (resolving crbug.com/371112531).

NTP Promos: Defensive improvements

Following a bugfix, add some extra protection against possible future
corner cases.

- Handle non-positive term and session limits explicitly, in case we ever want a promo to run indefinitely.
- Handle invalid promo IDs coming from WebUI, in case a stale NTP persists across a Chrome update that removes a promo.
- Add explicit Feature Parameter-loading test coverage
- Add a missing param declaration (for consistency)
- Boost documentation

Trim //chrome/test:unit_tests leaf deps (2/3)

Most unit_tests sources have moved into per-directory source_sets, but
the deps they needed stayed behind in chrome/test/BUILD.gn. Remove leaf
deps that the remaining sources no longer include. This is part 2 of 3;
the parts touch different regions of the unit_tests target and can land
in any order.

Kept: per-directory test aggregators and other test targets, test
support targets, Android Java deps, and non-C++ targets such as APK
assets (V8 snapshot, paks), resources, strings and generated headers,
since gn check doesn't cover them.

This is part of an effort to shrink chrome/test/BUILD.gn by moving test
sources into per-directory targets.

Flush stale detached timelines before InitClientAnimationState and AnimateLayers

When animation timelines are detached during an in-flight compositor
commit, AnimationHost::DetachAnimationTimeline() defers their removal
until RemoveStaleTimelines() is called. Previously, stale timelines and
triggers were only flushed in LayerTreeHost::WillCommit() and
LayerTreeHost::CommitComplete().

Because CommitComplete() is posted asynchronously to the main thread
after the commit completion event is signaled, a new document's paint
lifecycle or the next BeginMainFrame can run before CommitComplete() is
dequeued. This caused AnimationHost::InitClientAnimationState() to
iterate over stale ElementAnimations from the detached document against
rebuilt PropertyTrees, hitting a DCHECK in
PropertyTrees::ElementIsAnimatingChanged().

Flush RemoveStaleTimelines() in
AnimationHost::InitClientAnimationState() and flush both
RemoveStaleTimelines() and RemoveStaleTriggers() at the start of
LayerTreeHost::AnimateLayers().

guide as part of `updateSelectedCollectionViewItemRingAndBringIntoView`,
which is already called whenever the selection changes
post-initialization.

Fix re-entrant infobar removal during user interactions

When an infobar button or link is clicked, InfoBarView and
ConfirmInfoBar invoke the delegate callback synchronously and then call
RemoveSelf(). If the delegate callback or a synchronous tab switch
re-entrantly calls InfoBarManager::RemoveInfoBar() while animations are
disabled or after a tab switch hides the infobar, the InfoBar is deleted
while its interaction handler is still on the stack. Returning to
RemoveSelf() then dereferences the destroyed InfoBar and crashes in
InfoBarManager::RemoveInfoBarInternal().

To fix these lifetime and re-entrancy issues:
    - Track active delegate interactions in BrowserInfoBarManager so
      RemoveInfoBarWithoutResult() defers removal until control returns     to the view, rather than destroying the infobar mid-callback.
    - Claim pending results before invoking action callbacks and preserve pending link-click results across global infobar tab switches.
    - Skip moving global infobars to newly activated tabs when an instance is already in a closing interaction, and cascade global closure when an inline link interaction closes an already-detached instance.
    - Disarm global session restore infobars when the kIgnored result is
      reported.
    - Remove the StartupLaunchInfoBarDelegate::Accept() override, unregister delegate observers in CloseAllInfoBars(), and notify observers before updating startup prefs so the infobar is closed cleanly after Accept() returns rather than re-entrantly during observer iteration.

d7e2e936d9cc5b36b8933511a73d3d38e239c4f6 [ diff ] 
[xr] Remove SyncToken HasData() checks in ArCoreGl

Previously, ArCoreGl::FinishRenderingFrame() only added a buffer to
reclaimed_buffers if its reclaimed_sync_token.HasData() was true.
However, When UseAutomaticSyncTokenManagement is enabled (in the
future), the reclaimed_sync_token will always be empty since the actual
SyncToken will be stored and managed inside ClientSharedImage. As a
result, in the automatic SyncToken mode, FinishRenderingFrame() will
always leave reclaimed_buffers empty, and skip
CreateGpuFenceForSyncTokens(). This could cause the frame to be recycled
immediately while Viz is still reading its buffers.

To fix this issue, the current CL removes the HasData() checks for
reclaimed_sync_token so that any existing buffer on the frame is always
added to reclaimed_buffers.

This change does not break the existing behavior under manual SyncToken
mode: if a buffer has a valid reclaimed_sync_token, the flow is
unchanged; if its reclaimed_sync_token is empty, WaitSyncTokenCHROMIUM()
inside CreateGpuFenceForSyncTokens() becomes a no-op, and the frame
still finishes through OnReclaimedGpuFenceAvailable() ->
ClearRenderingFrame(). This change matches the unconditional
CreateGpuFenceForSyncTokens() calls in CardboardRenderLoop and
OpenXrRenderLoop.

commerce: Migrate DiscountsCouponCodeLabelView background to ui::ColorId

This CL simplifies `DiscountsCouponCodeLabelView` by installing its
rounded background once in the constructor. Previously, this view was
required to manually handle theme updates by overriding
`OnThemeChanged()`.

Following crrev.com/c/6313744, we can pass the `ui::ColorId` directly to
`views::CreateRoundedRectBackground()`. The background now automatically
handles theme changes, eliminating the need for manual color management.

f1e8aa1d1cf2d1c4e3ba4ddddd13e1d624c252bb [ diff ] 
[FontDataService] Test FontDataManager file-handle path on Linux/CrOS

Following https://review.skia.org/1314956, SkTypeface_FCI implements
onGetResourceName() on Linux and ChromeOS, so FontDataServiceImpl now
shares font file handles natively (see https://crrev.com/c/8085813).

However, TestFontServiceApp in FontDataManagerUnitTest still defaulted
use_memory_fallback_ to true on Linux and ChromeOS, causing the
FontDataManager unit tests to exercise the shared-memory region fallback
rather than the memory-mapped file path.

This CL defaults use_memory_fallback_ to false across all platforms, and
parameterizes FontDataManagerUnitTest over use_memory_fallback to
exercise both the file-handle and shared-memory fallback paths across
the test suite, replacing the standalone
MatchFamilyStyleWithMemoryRegion test

[media] Remove the kPauseBackgroundTimer kill switch and idle pause timer

WebMediaPlayerImpl used to pause a suspended, audible player five
seconds after its page or frame was hidden. crrev.com/c/6465855 put
that timer behind kPauseBackgroundTimer, disabled by default, after
reports that the timer had stopped working some time ago, and asked
for the flag to be removed in M140 once two stable releases had
shipped without it.

Seventeen milestones later the flag was never re-enabled. Remove the
flag, ScheduleIdlePauseTimer() with its two callers, the
background_pause_timer_ member, the four places that stopped the
timer, and the test that enabled the flag to exercise it.

PauseReason::kSuspendedPlayerIdleTimeout is no longer produced by the
player. It stays in the public WebMediaPlayer API and in
HTMLMediaElement for now; removing it there can be a follow-up.

R=dalecurtis@chromium.org

Bind AppMenuItemProperties.SHORTCUT_TEXT and propagate the enabled state
in IncognitoMenuItemViewBinder.bind() so that Incognito 3-dot menu items

layout_weight=1 so long titles ellipsize cleanly without clipping the
shortcut text.

Fix ScopedFeatureList race in MediaStreamVideoCapturerSourceTest

This CL moves `ScopedFeatureList` into
`MediaStreamVideoCapturerSourceTest` before `platform_` so the IO thread
is joined before `~ScopedFeatureList()` restores the global
`FeatureList`. This fixes TSan/ASan teardown races responsible for
~2,200 direct test failures/crashes (~16,200 batch-poisoned test
failures) per week.

[FRE][Android] Only skip the welcome page once the user moved past it

When a user taps "Continue as <account>" in FRE, acceptTermsOfService()
is called early in proceedWithSignIn() to enable crash/metrics
reporting for the sign-in network request. This used to also set the
FIRST_RUN_SKIP_WELCOME_PAGE shared preference to true.

If sign-in was then interrupted (e.g. the enterprise management dialog
was cancelled, sign-in failed offline, or the app was killed while the
management notice was shown), FIRST_RUN_SKIP_WELCOME_PAGE remained
true. On the next launch, FirstRunActivity skipped
SigninFirstRunFragment, had no other pages to show, and marked the
entire FRE flow complete. This allowed the user to enter the browser
signed out even when forced sign-in policy (BrowserSignin = 2) was
active.

This CL stops setting FIRST_RUN_SKIP_WELCOME_PAGE when the ToS is
accepted. Instead, it is updated in setCurrentItemForPager(), which
every FRE page transition goes through: it is set to true when moving
past the welcome page (including when the FRE completes right after
it) and reset to false when navigating back to it. It is also still set
in exitFirstRun() to preserve the existing behavior when the FRE is
skipped by the TosDialogBehavior policy.

parent
c1ae152427605ce404f4b76425c693b4b1db61b8 [ diff ] 
[iOS] Preserve restored NTP scroll position on content size updates

crrev.com/c/8487454 started notifying -[NewTabPageCoordinator
contentSuggestionsWasUpdated] whenever the Most Visited Tiles
collection view's content size changes. That calls
-[NewTabPageViewController updateHeightAboveFeed], which shifts the
current content offset by the change in height above the feed.

When returning to the NTP, the restored scroll position is applied
before the Most Visited Tiles finish their async layout (e.g. a newly
visited site is added as a tile). The resulting updateHeightAboveFeed
calls shift the offset by deltas that can be lost to clamping in
-setContentOffset:, which leaves the NTP scrolled to the top instead
of at the restored position.

hasSavedOffsetFromPreviousScrollState is kept YES after a restore
specifically so that async Content Suggestions updates do not override
the restored position (see -viewDidAppear: and
-feedLayoutDidEndUpdatesWithType:). Honor it in updateHeightAboveFeed
by re-applying the saved offset while it is set.

This fixes NTPHomeTestCase/testPositionRestoredWithoutShiftingOffset
on ios-fieldtrial-rel, where ChromeNextIa is disabled.

media: Re-enable AV1 support for PlayReady SL3000 on Windows

Re-enabled AV1 support for PlayReady SL3000 on Windows since:
- the AV1 decoding error is addressed on Edge.
- the AV1 decoding hang / black screen issue is addressed on Chrome.

This AV1 support will be on M156+.

Next steps:
- Microsoft to finish testing and release the new AV1 codec
  (v2.0.35.0+).
- Chrome to re-enable AV1 now on M157 Canary.
- Work with partners to run small tests on Chrome M157+ to confirm if
  AV1 decoding issues are addressed.

* Makes the nested Properties classes of immutable, with constructors, so that non-null fields are always set.

  mContentView, and updates tests to pass initialized members.

Java->Native calls.

[Autofill] Re-enable disabled KeyboardAccessoryViewTest tests on Desktop

Five tests in KeyboardAccessoryViewTest were disabled on Desktop Android
due to failures under Batch.PER_CLASS. In freeform/desktop multi-window
environments, ViewUtils.onViewWaiting defaulted to
RootSpec.focusedRoot(), timing out when window focus was not held by the
primary activity window. Additionally, test trackers were not plumbed to
the accessory view, KeyboardAccessoryView defaulted to Gravity.TOP |
Gravity.START overlapping the desktop caption bar, and help bubble
dismissal clicks raced with window surface settlement.

* Introduce onActivityViewWaiting helper using ViewFinder.waitForView to
  resolve views in the test activity's window without requiring global
  window focus.
* Initialize FeatureEngagementTracker on the accessory view in
  provider.whenLoaded to ensure test trackers are properly plumbed.
* Set docked STYLE
  (KeyboardAccessoryStyle.createDockedKeyboardAccessoryStyle(0)) in
  setUp() so KeyboardAccessoryView docks to Gravity.BOTTOM (matching
  production KeyboardAccessoryMediator) rather than defaulting to
  Gravity.TOP | Gravity.START inside the desktop caption bar.
* Update waitForHelpBubble to use ViewFinder.waitForView with
  ViewElement.initialSettleTimeOption(500) so the PopupWindow surface
  and FLAG_WATCH_OUTSIDE_TOUCH input handle settle in
  SurfaceFlinger/InputDispatcher before clicking.
* Use CriteriaHelper.pollUiThread for asynchronous bubble dismissals and
  event emissions to eliminate UI thread timing races.
* Re-enable the 5 disabled tests on Desktop Android.

parent
d0357ab1bcb544f1d44f4a0d1ced6a3887e7bc5c [ diff ] 
Don't suspend the screensaver for kPreventAppSuspension on Linux

PowerSaveBlocker on Linux suspended the platform screensaver for every
WakeLockType, including kPreventAppSuspension, which should keep the
system awake while still allowing the display to dim and sleep.

On Wayland, suspending the screensaver creates a zwp_idle_inhibitor_v1
on the focused window, which prevents the display from going idle while
the window is visible. As a result, audio-only playback (and other
kPreventAppSuspension users such as downloads and WebRTC) kept the
display awake unless the window was minimized. On native X11 the
XScreenSaver suspension similarly disabled DPMS blanking. This became
widely visible when Wayland became the default in M141; previously
Chrome ran under XWayland, where the X11 suspension has no effect on the
compositor.

Only suspend the screensaver for the display wake lock types. System
suspend for kPreventAppSuspension is still inhibited via the D-Bus
session/power management APIs.

net: Generate SSPI auth tokens off the network sequence

HttpAuthSSPI::GenerateAuthToken() ran AcquireCredentialsHandle() and
InitializeSecurityContext() inline on the network sequence and
discarded the callback it was handed, stalling every socket in the
network service for the duration of the call -- however long Windows
takes, measured at 15s on one client where Negotiate waited on an
unreachable KDC before falling back to NTLM. Move the SSPI calls to a
per-handler blocking sequence and complete through the callback
HttpAuthMechanism already provides. SSPILibrary's cached max token
length is lock-guarded so that independent handshakes do not serialize
behind each other.

AuthLibrary is refcounted on all non-Android platforms, including
GSSAPILibrary on POSIX, so the handler factory carries a single
ownership model. On POSIX this is groundwork for making HttpAuthGSSAPI
asynchronous (crbug.com/565047697); it is still synchronous here.

R=bashi@chromium.org, seblalancette@chromium.org

Bug: 561613776
Test: net_unittests --gtest_filter=HttpAuthSSPI*:HttpAuthHandlerNegotiateTest.*:HttpAuthGSSAPI*

[Code Health] Spanify SkBitmap access in x11_cursor_loader.cc

Replace the UNSAFE_TODO memcpy and raw base::span construction over
SkBitmap::getPixels() in XCursorLoader::CreateCursor() and
ParseCursorFile() with gfx::SkPixmapToSpan() and
gfx::SkPixmapToWritableSpan(). CreateCursor() now constructs
base::RefCountedBytes directly from the pixel span instead of copying
through an intermediate std::vector.

Both helpers size the span with SkPixmap::computeByteSize(), which is
what SkBitmap::computeByteSize() forwards to, so there is no behavior
change.

Extend XCursorLoaderTest.BestSize to verify that every pixel of the
selected 2x2 image is copied in row-major order.

[OptimizationGuide] Decompose asset policy and DiskSpaceStatus

DiskSpaceStatus previously mixed cached free-disk-space state with
unrelated feature-flag and battery-power policy checks in
CanSupportProactiveDownload(), while ManifestAssetManager::ShouldInstall()
combined initial registration eligibility, retention of
already-registered assets, and foreground download criteria into a
single overloaded predicate alongside inline priority checks in
UpdateRegistrations(). Separate DiskSpaceStatus (disk-space measurement
and thresholds) from ManifestAssetManager policy and decompose
ShouldInstall() into single-purpose predicates to clarify the distinct
policy rules governing each stage of component reconciliation.

Refactoring:
* Restrict DiskSpaceStatus to free-space caching and disk threshold
  queries (IsSufficientForOnDemandInstall() and
  IsSufficientForBackgroundInstall()), moving feature-flag and battery
  power checks into ManifestAssetManager::CanSupportProactiveDownload().
* Decompose ShouldInstall() and inline priority checks into named
  predicates: ShouldRetain(), ShouldRegisterNewVersion(),
  ShouldInstallOrRetain(), and ShouldRequestForegroundDownload().
* Remove dead ManifestAssetManager::GetBrokerProperties().

Behavioral changes: None.

[PM] Make process priority part of the PriorityVotingSystem

Adds ProcessNode as a VoteContext. Voters can vote directly on a
process. Only renderer processes can be voted on.

The ProcessPriorityAggregator is now owned by the PriorityVotingSystem
instead of being installed separately. Instead of setting the priority
of a process directly, it casts it as a vote on the process, where it is
aggregated with the votes cast directly on the process. The resulting
priorities are unchanged.

The PriorityVotingSystem must now be added to the graph before any node
(CHECKed).

[MiraclePtr] Add RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION in D3D12VideoEncodeDecodedPictureBuffers

This change adds `RAW_PTR_EXCLUSION` to the `raw_resources_` container
in `D3D12VideoEncodeDecodedPictureBuffers`. The container uses
`ID3D12Resource*`and is used for OS structure interop with the D3D12
API,meaning we cannot easily replace its elements with `raw_ptr<T>`.

This exclusion is necessary to prevent compiler errors from the upcoming
clang-plugin update that will strictly ban un-rewritten instances of raw
C-style pointers in templated containers, as part of the broader
MiraclePtr safety initiative.

WebUILocationBar: Synchronously update omnibox focus state in SetFocus

DiceMigrationServiceForcedMigrationInteractiveUiTest.
ToastDoesNotCloseOnTabSwitch fails on Mac with WebUILocationBar enabled
when switching back to a tab where the omnibox was focused (e.g.
about:blank).

There were two interrelated asynchronous timing issues during fast tab
switching:

1. Focus storage during rapid tab switches:
   When switching away from a tab where focus was requested for the
   omnibox, ChromeWebContentsViewFocusHelper::StoreFocus() only saves
   the WebUI toolbar view if location_bar->IsFocusWithin() is true.
   Previously, WebUILocationBar::PropagateFocusRequest() relied on an
   asynchronous Mojo IPC from the WebUI renderer to set
   SetFocusWithin(true). In fast tab switches (such as in tests), the
   IPC had not yet arrived, so StoreFocus() failed to save the
   focused view. Consequently, when switching back to the tab,
   WebContentsViewMac::RestoreFocus found no stored focus in
   ChromeWebContentsViewFocusHelper and fell back to
   SetInitialFocus(), which called SetFocusToLocationBar() for
   about:blank.

2. Asynchronous OmniboxEditModel focus notification race with
   ToastController:
   In Browser::OnActiveTabChanged, window_->OnActiveTabChanged()
   restores focus (or sets initial focus) to the newly active tab
   before did_active_tab_change_callback_list_ notifies
   ToastController::OnActiveTabChanged to observe the tab's
   OmniboxTabHelper. With OmniboxViewViews, focusing synchronously
   updates OmniboxEditModel::OnSetFocus(false) before ToastController
   starts observing. With WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox, SetFocusWithTarget()
   only sent an asynchronous Mojo request and waited for
   OnFocusChange() from the renderer to call OnSetFocus(false).
   Because the Mojo IPC arrived after ToastController subscribed to
   the new tab's OmniboxTabHelper,
   ToastController::OnOmniboxFocusChanged treated it as a new focus
   event and dismissed the toast widget.

This CL resolves both issues:

1. Calls SetFocusWithin(true) synchronously in
   WebUILocationBar::PropagateFocusRequest() (when the toolbar's
   internal WebView already has focus) so
   ChromeWebContentsViewFocusHelper::StoreFocus() correctly saves the
   focus state even if tab switching happens before the renderer IPC.
   WebUILocationBar::SetFocusWithin() now also early-returns when the
   state is unchanged, so the later renderer IPC does not re-notify
   LocationBar::Observers for a focus change that was already applied.
2. Guards WebUIToolbarWebView::OnLocationBarFocusWithinChanged() so a
   focused=true IPC from the renderer is ignored if web_view_ no longer
   has focus. Since the browser-side state is now set synchronously, a
   late-arriving focus IPC (e.g. after focus has already moved during a
   tab switch) would otherwise incorrectly mark the location bar as
   focused. Blur (focused=false) IPCs are still always processed.
3. Updates has_focus_ and calls OmniboxEditModel::OnSetFocus(false)
   synchronously in WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::SetFocusWithTarget() (when
   !kWebUIOmniboxFullPopup), and guards OnSetFocus() in OnFocusChange()
   with if (!has_focus_).
4. Adds unit tests in WebUILocationBarTest (SetFocusWithin
   deduplication and the OnLocationBarFocusWithinChanged guard) and
   WebUIReadOnlyOmniboxTest.

[Code Health] Spanify ui/gtk/gtk_util.cc

Replace unsafe strcmp calls in GtkInitFromCommandLine and
AppendCssNodeToStyleContext with std::string_view comparisons (using
base::StringTokenizer::token_piece() to avoid temporary string
allocations), and wrap the Cairo image surface pixel buffer in
base::span<const SkColor> in CairoSurface::GetAveragePixelValue.

The span's size of width * height pixels is only valid if the surface
stride is exactly 4 * width, so the existing DCHECK on that invariant is
upgraded to a CHECK. This cannot fire for surfaces created by
CairoSurface, which always use the ARGB32 stride.

[Blink] Preserve terminal kClosed state in DelegatingBytesConsumer

BytesConsumer requires that once a consumer reaches a terminal state
(kClosed or kErrored), its state must never change. However,
ResponseBodyLoader::DelegatingBytesConsumer::GetPublicState() previously
checked `loader_->IsAborted()` before checking whether the consumer had
already reached `State::kDone`, `State::kCancelled`, or `kClosed`.

When a teed fetch() response body (`TeeHelper` wrapping
`DelegatingBytesConsumer`) finished reading all bytes from the data
pipe, `TeeHelper::Destination::EndRead()` observed `PublicState::kClosed`
and posted `Destination::Close()` asynchronously. If the loader was
aborted before `Destination::Close()` ran, `GetPublicState()` flipped
retroactively from `kClosed` to `kErrored`, triggering a DCHECK failure
in `TeeHelper::Destination::Close()` (`kClosed vs. kErrored`).

Preserve `PublicState::kClosed` (and `Result::kDone` in `BeginRead()`)
once `DelegatingBytesConsumer` has reached `State::kDone` or
`State::kCancelled`, and check `is_closed_ || is_cancelled_` before the
DCHECKs in `TeeHelper::Destination::Close()`.

[permissions] Skip removed subscriptions in PermissionResultChange()

When a subscription callback removes another subscription belonging to
the same notification batch, base::IDMap defers deleting the entry
if an iterator is active (e.g. during re-entrant notifications or status
checks). In that case, the removed subscription's entry remains in
memory and its WeakPtr is not invalidated, but Lookup() returns null.
This previously caused a CHECK failure when delivering the change.

Instead of relying on WeakPtr to detect unsubscribed listeners, check
subscriptions_.Lookup() directly in PermissionResultChange() and
return early if the subscription is not found. This handles both
immediate and deferred IDMap deletion uniformly and allows dropping
the WeakPtr logic on PermissionResultSubscription.

Trim //chrome/test:unit_tests leaf deps (1/3)

Most unit_tests sources have moved into per-directory source_sets, but
the deps they needed stayed behind in chrome/test/BUILD.gn. Remove leaf
deps that the remaining sources no longer include. This is part 1 of 3;
the parts touch different regions of the unit_tests target and can land
in any order.

Kept: per-directory test aggregators and other test targets, test
support targets, Android Java deps, and non-C++ targets such as APK
assets (V8 snapshot, paks), resources, strings and generated headers,
since gn check doesn't cover them.

This is part of an effort to shrink chrome/test/BUILD.gn by moving test
sources into per-directory targets.

Verification, for this CL alone and for all 3 parts together:
- gn check passes on Linux (debug and release), ChromeOS, ChromeOS
  device (betty), Windows (x64 and x86), Mac, Android desktop and
  Android phone.

Fix DCHECK crash on PageContentStore non-catastrophic errors

The `Database` class has two main ways of closing a database: `Close()`
and `Poison()`. `Close()` should only be used for clean shutdowns, after
all statements finished executing. This is enforced using DCHECKs
detecting if `Close()` is called out-of-line (e.g. [1]).

If the database client wishes to close the database from within the
error callback, it must do so using `Poison()` since the error callback
can be called from anywhere, while there are still statements open and
active.

[1]:
https://crsrc.org/c/sql/database.cc;l=634-638;drc=7e6555a151577feb361361919d85a5477b1e88ca

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for omnibox_popup_resource_budget_browsertest

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

[glic] Run device status checks for permission overrides

When an embedder overrides a permission result to GRANTED (such as for
PrivilegedWebContents), PermissionManager bypassed permission contexts
entirely. On Android, this skipped OS runtime permission reprompts and
system location (LSD) dialogs, causing location requests to fail.

* Route GRANTED overrides to the permission context when the context
  requires device status checks (AlwaysIncludeDeviceStatus).
* Add PermissionContextBase::RequestPermissionWithResultOverride and
  implement it in GeolocationPermissionContextAndroid to trigger OS
  and system location prompts without modifying HostContentSettingsMap.
* Update PermissionManager::GetPermissionStatusInternal to include
  device status checks for overridden results.
* Add unit test in GeolocationPermissionContextTests.

Reland "[Actor] Preserve last actuated tab ID on ActorTask after native destruction"

This is a reland of commit a5a2357dbb21aa9779de54debfc2ea5a98bc2fe1

Reason for revert:
crrev.com/c/8500434 reverted the original CL due to a crash in
clearNativePtr(). ActorTaskAndroid is stored as SupportsUserData::Data
on ActorTask, so ~ActorTaskAndroid() ran inside ~SupportsUserData()
after ~ActorTask() had already completed and after ~ActorTaskAndroid()
zeroed task_. Making JNI calls back into ActorTaskAndroid from
clearNativePtr() therefore dereferenced a null/destroyed native task.

Fix:
- Call ClearAllUserData() in ActorTask::~ActorTask() so
  ActorTaskAndroid is destroyed while ActorTask fields are still alive.
- Call Java_ActorTask_clearNativePtr() before resetting task_ = nullptr
  in ActorTaskAndroid::~ActorTaskAndroid() so clearNativePtr() can
  safely snapshot mLastKnownState, mLastKnownActuatedTabId, and
  mLastKnownTargetTabId before nulling mNativeTask.

Original change's description:
> [Actor] Preserve last actuated tab ID on ActorTask after native destruction
>
> When an ActorTask completes, the native ActorTask is destroyed on the
> next UI message-loop tick after notifying observers, zeroing
> ActorTask.mNativeTask via clearNativePtr().
>
> When a terminal live notification is later demoted to a regular
> dismissible notification, rebuilding the notification from the Java
> ActorTask caused getLastActuatedTabId() and getTargetTabId() to return
> Tab.INVALID_TAB_ID (-1), overwriting BRING_TAB_TO_FRONT on the system
> PendingIntent and breaking tab and conversation routing on click.
>
> Cache mLastKnownActuatedTabId on the Java ActorTask so
> getLastActuatedTabId() and getTargetTabId() honor their documented
> post-completion contract.

[Direct Offers] Don't keep WebContents ptr in AutofillFieldPromoViewImpl

`AutofillFieldPromoViewImpl` is added as a child of the browser window's
contents view, so it is owned by the browser window, not the tab. Since
`AutofillFieldPromoControllerImpl::Hide()` closes the view in a posted
task, the view outlives the `WebContents` when the tab is closed while
the field IPH is showing. The view's `raw_ptr<content::WebContents>` is
then dangling when the view is destroyed, which crashes builds with
dangling pointer checks enabled.

The `WebContents` is only needed to compute the view bounds in the
constructor, so pass it to `SetViewBounds()` instead of storing it.

Fix crash in PageContentStore database recovery

The PageContentStore database registers an error callback to be invoked
on SQLite errors. If a catastrophic error is detected, the callback
attempts a database recovery. If that succeeds, it immediately tries to
re-initialize the database. This crashes unconditionally because
`InitializeDb()` does `CHECK(!db_initialized_)` and `db_initialized_` is
`true` when the error callback is invoked. This crash is observed in
production Crash data.

The fix here is just to not try to re-open the database. If reopening
was necessary, it should be done by having the error callback schedule a
task to re-open the database later. Re-opening from within the error
callback is not a good idea and we are considering banning this
entirely. The client code cannot possibly make sense of a database
closing and re-opening in the middle of transactions. This would revert
the first part of the transaction and let the rest execute in
autocommit mode after the database was re-opened.

[PM] PriorityVotingSystem: make the MaxVoteAggregator the hub

Replaces RootVoteObserver. The PriorityVotingSystem now owns the
MaxVoteAggregator, and the top vote of a node in the aggregator is its
final priority:

- Every vote goes into the MaxVoteAggregator through a VotingChannel.
- MaxVoteAggregator::Observer is notified when the top vote of a node
  changes. The PrioritySetter observes it and sets the priority of
  frames and workers (InheritClientPriorityVoter uses it for its own
  aggregator too).
- The aggregator supports re-entrant votes, and CHECKs that the top vote
  of a node doesn't change while its observers are being notified,
  which catches cycles.

This prepares for process and page votes, which will be cast back into
the MaxVoteAggregator.

Also adds CHECKs that no votes are leaked on removed nodes, and fixes
the priority reason of a worker whose last vote is removed, which was
reset to FrameNodeImpl::kDefaultPriorityReason.

Add ZeroLimitPolicy to the MemoryCoordinator

Adds ZeroLimitPolicy, which sets the memory limit of all stateful
MemoryConsumers (traits.is_stateful == IsStateful::kYes) to zero (0%)
and requests memory release.

This policy is gated behind the kMemoryCoordinatorZeroLimit feature flag
(disabled by default) and is intended for Finch experimentation to
determine the upper-bound potential impact of the MemoryCoordinator on
system and process metrics.

Because the BrowserMemoryCoordinatorImpl is created before the
FeatureList is initialized, feature-gated policies are instantiated
through a new InitializePolicies() method. It is called by
ContentMainRunnerImpl right after PostEarlyInitialization(), and by the
equivalent Android code path in BrowserTestBase.

Disable subframe error page isolation on Cast

Isolating subframe error pages requires out-of-process iframes. Cast
already avoids out-of-process iframes by not enabling strict site
isolation in
CastContentBrowserClient::ShouldEnableStrictSiteIsolation(), and
similarly to low-end Android devices (https://crrev.com/c/8489916),
subframe error page isolation is not really needed on Cast, so this CL
turns it off. Without this change, subframe errors would start creating
out-of-process iframes on Cast once IsolateSubframeErrorPages is enabled
by default, which we probably don't want.

To do this, override ShouldIsolateErrorPage() to only isolate main frame
error pages on Cast. This preserves the current behavior and is similar
to what was done on headless (see
HeadlessContentBrowserClient::ShouldIsolateErrorPage()).

4dbfe4ef42a60627ef0037b1e2e53e88e39ae229
parent
b2544213f47a1941625e87315872b2aec7acbd80 [ diff ] 
Detect already-loaded pages in StartupObserver

StartupObserver only checked whether a page had finished loading when
the page's loading state changed. A page that finishes loading before it
becomes a visible tab doesn't change loading state again when it's
shown, so the observer kept its StartupInProgressRef until the failsafe
timeout (3 minutes by default), delaying after-startup tasks. For
example, this happens if the user minimizes the window, or switches to a
background tab that already finished loading, while the first tab is
still loading.

Check the loading state whenever a page might become interesting (when
it's added, becomes visible or becomes a tab), not only when its loading
state changes.

With kImprovedStartupBestEffortDelay enabled, also stop waiting if every
interesting page is hidden or closed before one finishes loading, for
example if the window stays minimized. Track all interesting pages, and
when the last one goes away, restart the timeout that's used when no
visible tab appears, and log the new kVisiblePagesHidden reason if it
expires. A page that becomes interesting again stops the timeout, so
switching tabs, which hides the old tab before showing the new one,
doesn't end startup.

Also extend the expiry of Startup.BrowserStartupCompleteReason, which
logs the new reason, to 2027-10-06.

Tested by StartupObserverTest cases in unit_tests for tabs that finish
loading before they're shown, and for tabs that are hidden, closed or
switched while loading, with kImprovedStartupBestEffortDelay disabled
and in each of its configurations.

Replace base::WrapUnique/new with std::make_unique in extensions, net

Follow the Chromium style guide preference for std::make_unique over
base::WrapUnique(new T(...)) and std::unique_ptr<T>(new T(...)): it
avoids naming the type twice and avoids the ambiguity between new Foo
and new Foo(), which mean different things for types without a
user-defined constructor.

[iOS][Autofill] Populate form_control_ax_id and share DOM node ID pool

To support extracting neighbourhood context from AnnotatedPageContent on
iOS:
1. Populate FormFieldData::form_control_ax_id from the field's
   renderer_id in ExtractFormFieldData.
2. Share the per-document node ID pool (__gCrUniqueID) between Autofill
   (renderer_id.ts) and APC DOM node ID extraction (dom_node_ids.ts) so
   that a form control's common_ancestor_dom_node_id in APC matches its
   FormFieldData::form_control_ax_id without collisions.

[histogram-cleanup] Remove expired histogram: Views.LayoutCallDepth

This removes the Views.LayoutCallDepth histogram, which expired on
2025-07-06 and was never extended, so nothing is collecting or reading
it anymore. It was recorded at the end of View::LayoutImmediately()
from a reentrancy counter and a running maximum, and those two members
existed only to feed this metric, so they go away along with the
recording call and the histogram's entry in the ui histograms.xml. The
neighboring Views.InvalidatesDuringLayout metric is not expired and is
left alone.

OBSOLETE_HISTOGRAM[Views.LayoutCallDepth]=expired

This change was generated using the skill histogram-cleanup.

[Actor] Reuse about:blank initiator tabs in ActorKeyedService::CreateActorTab

CreateActorTab already reuses the initiator tab instead of opening a new
one when the initiator is showing the NTP. Extend the same treatment to
about:blank so that empty tabs are not left behind when an actor task is
started from one.

non-empty page path that still opens a new tab.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for cv_display_link_mac

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

rewriting to `raw_ptr` was performed.

[WebAudio] Fix flake in audioworkletprocessor-gc.https.html

After CL 7750233 removed `await context.close()` prior to the worklet
GC check, `node2`'s disposed `AudioHandler` could remain in
`DeferredTaskHandler`'s orphan/automatic-pull lists when
`internals.audioHandlerCount()` was evaluated, causing it to flakily
return 3 instead of 2.

Changes:
- Call `await asyncGC()` and `await context.close()` after verifying
  `internals.audioWorkletProcessorCount()` and before asserting
  `internals.audioHandlerCount()`.
- Remove flaky test expectations for
  `webaudio/internals/audioworkletprocessor-gc.https.html`.

Remove content size override in ScopedTraitOverrider destructor

ScopedTraitOverrider read the view controller's effective
`preferredContentSizeCategory` in its constructor and set it back as a
trait override in its destructor. Instead of reverting the override,
this pinned the view controller to the size read at construction time
for the rest of the app process, so later text size changes in the
same process were ignored.

Record the view controller's content size category override instead
(`nil` if it has none), then restore that override or remove it with
`removeTrait:`.

Also document the restore-or-remove contract and mark the constructor
`explicit`.

[mac] Remove the expired Mac.AppCodeSignClone* histograms

CodeSignCloneManager recorded five histograms about the code sign
clone: Mac.AppHardLinkError, Mac.AppClonefileError,
Mac.AppCodeSignCloneCount, Mac.AppCodeSignCloneExists and
Mac.AppCodeSignCloneCreationTime. All of them expired between
2025-08-03 and 2025-10-05, so the code that records them is dead.

Some of that code did work only for the metrics. RecordCloneCount()
called getattrlist() on the clone temp dir after each clone, and the
clone exists timer woke up once a day to check that the clone's main
executable and Info.plist were still there, recording the result and
stopping once they were gone. Remove both, together with the recording
helpers, the MacCloneExists enum, the Info.plist path constant that
only the existence check used, and the timing around the clone.
Cloning and cleanup are unchanged.

Also remove the histograms.xml entries and the MacCloneExists enum.
MacErrno stays, other histograms still use it.

R=avi@chromium.org

Sanitize cross-origin URLs in UpdateRendererOnMixedContentFound()

UpdateRendererOnMixedContentFound() notifies the navigating frame's
current RenderFrameHost, which hosts the pre-navigation document. That
document can be cross-origin with both the navigation target URL and
the pre-redirect URL (e.g. embedder-initiated navigations or history
traversals), and Blink forwards url_before_redirects into CSP mixed
content violation reports.

Strip URLs not chosen by a same-origin initiator or redirector to
their origin when cross-origin with the receiving RenderFrameHost.

parent
76a9e5ddf3de5e65c610470a2e68aa23366659a8 [ diff ] 
[DynamicPatching] Extract InstallProductComponent

Extract the Windows product component installation logic from
PlatformRuntimeComponentInstallerPolicy into a shared
component_updater::InstallProductComponent helper so that it can be
reused by other product-scoped components (such as the dynamic patch
component).

InstallProductComponent installs a .crx3 payload into the Chrome
installation directory:
- For system-level installs on Windows, it invokes an elevated
  AppCommand via IAppCommandWeb: install-component with the inner CRX
  path (%1) or, if a User Data directory is provided,
  install-component-for-user with the inner CRX path (%1) and the
  canonicalized User Data directory (%2). It polls until the command
  completes.
- For per-user installs on Windows, it launches setup.exe with
  --install-component and --udd (if provided) and waits for it to exit.
- On other platforms, a stub returns kLaunchFailed for now.

As with PlatformRuntime's installation today, there is no timeout.

A User Data directory is canonicalized with
child_module::CanonicalizeUserDataDir(), since setup derives the
component's destination from it without accessing it. Installation
fails without running setup if it cannot be canonicalized.

ProductComponentInstallResult distinguishes the same failure modes that
PlatformRuntime reports (missing command, Chrome not installed, internal
setup failures, and COM/RPC errors).
PlatformRuntimeComponentInstallerPolicy now delegates to
InstallProductComponent and maps each result to its existing
PlatformRuntimeInstallationResult, retaining the managed device and
network path breakdown of internal failures, so that
ComponentUpdater.PlatformRuntime.InstallationResult.* is unchanged.
PlatformRuntime's unit tests are unchanged and continue to verify this
end-to-end. install_product_component_unittest.cc tests the helper
itself, including command selection, parameter passing, and User Data
directory canonicalization.

parent
ac7125bb6f05c3bf30f541db5888da9e3832d9fe [ diff ] 
viz: Read software copies directly into the blit destination

For a CopyOutputRequest with a BlitRequest into a client provided
SharedImage (e.g. the view transition capture of the outgoing document
of a cross-document navigation), SoftwareRenderer reads the render pass
into an intermediate N32 bitmap, and then draws that bitmap into the
destination SharedImage with kSrc, unscaled, at an integer offset.

When the copy is unscaled, isn't letterboxed, has no blend bitmaps, and
the destination is 8-bit premul in the same color space as the render
pass, this reads the pixels directly into the destination instead,
which produces the same pixels without the intermediate allocation,
copy and draw. Otherwise, the existing path is used.

Measured locally (linux, software compositing), this halves the cost of
the view transition capture copies in viz (6.7 ms -> 3.35 ms on the
test page) and makes the reveal of the incoming document ~2.4 ms
earlier. Navigation start to FCP doesn't change yet, since the first
frame of the incoming document is currently not on the same critical
path. This only affects software compositing; GPU compositing uses a
different path.

This is a performance change only and the output is identical, so the
existing ReadbackPixelTestRGBAWithBlit tests cover it. They now also run
with the feature disabled, to keep covering the general path.

Kill switch: SoftwareReadbackIntoBlitDestination.

Keep Assistant container presented on keyboard inset updates

Observe `fullscreenDidUpdateState:` (instead of
`fullscreenWillUpdateState:`) and track the last bottom fullscreen
progress in `AssistantContainerCoordinator` under
`kFullscreenRefactoring`, as `AssistantContainerCoordinator` does not
contribute obscured insets to `FullscreenBrowserAgent` and only reads
the final `bottom_progress()`.

Unlike the legacy `FullscreenUIUpdater` (which only forwards progress
changes), `FullscreenBrowserAgent` can also broadcast `DidUpdateState`
while `bottom_progress()` has not changed (e.g. when
`SetKeyboardObscuredInset` updates `insets.bottom`). Ignoring state
updates where `bottom_progress()` has not changed prevents re-applying
an unchanged progress of 0.0 and unexpectedly minimizing and hiding an
Assistant container that was presented while toolbars were collapsed.

Also guard `applyPanelLayoutConstraints` and
`applySheetLayoutConstraints` in `AssistantContainerViewController` when
trait changes fire before `didMoveToParentViewController:` creates the
parent-relative bottom constraints.

[Autofill] Hide suggestions on browser-side focus change

Suggestions are currently hidden only via `DidEndTextFieldEditing()`,
which Blink dispatches for <input> elements but not for <textarea> or
contenteditable elements. When the signal is missing, the Android
keyboard accessory keeps `FillingSource::AUTOFILL` registered after
focus has left the field and later asserts SHOULD_EXTEND_KEYBOARD in
`ManualFillingMediator`.

`BrowserAutofillManager` now hides suggestions with `kFocusChanged` when
the renderer reports focus on a non-form field, or on a form field other
than the one the suggestions were queried for.

The new behavior is behind `kAutofillHideSuggestionsOnFocusChange`
(disabled by default) and will be rolled out via a short Finch
experiment to confirm there is no regression before launching it.

VT: Don't snap zero-height browser controls for a VT

When a view transition captures the outgoing document of a
cross-document navigation, it snaps the browser controls to fully
shown, because they are animated to shown during the navigation.
Without browser controls, this has no effect on the page, but
it changes the shown ratio in the browser controls metadata of the
capture frame, which forces a new LocalSurfaceId for that frame.

This only snaps the browser controls if their total height is > 0.

This makes a difference in software compositing

Fix ExternalProtocolHandlerBrowserTest hang on Windows shutdown

ExternalProtocolHandlerBrowserTest navigates to mailto: URLs, which
triggers platform_util::OpenExternal(). On Windows,
OpenExternalOnWorkerThread() did not check
platform_util::internal::AreShellOperationsAllowed() (unlike
ShowItemInFolderOnWorkerThread(), platform_util::OpenItem(), and the
Linux implementation of OpenExternal()), nor did OpenExternal() use
TaskShutdownBehavior::CONTINUE_ON_SHUTDOWN. Additionally,
ExternalProtocolHandlerBrowserTest did not call
platform_util::internal::DisableShellOperationsForTesting().

As a result, ShellExecuteA() attempted to launch the OS default mail
handler on a ThreadPool worker thread during the browser test and hung
TaskEnvironment::CompleteShutdown for over 30 seconds.

Check AreShellOperationsAllowed() in OpenExternalOnWorkerThread(), use
CONTINUE_ON_SHUTDOWN in OpenExternal() and ShowItemInFolder(), and
disable shell operations in ExternalProtocolHandlerBrowserTest.

6d9ad99f14c5e39462903758e4a2ecce5bc382fe [ diff ] 
media: Wrap the VoiceIsolation STFT in BufferedVoiceIsolation

VoiceIsolation::CreateComponent() now wraps the StftVoiceIsolation stage
in a BufferedVoiceIsolation, so the returned component consumes the
10 ms frames (480 samples at 48 kHz) delivered by APM, while the STFT
keeps running on 20 ms frames.

The ConvertingAudioFifos in VoiceIsolationImpl now convert 480 frames
into 480 frames, so they only do channel mixing. The rebuffering moved
from the forward FIFO into BufferedVoiceIsolation, and the latency for
10 ms input is unchanged. A follow-up CL replaces the FIFOs with
ChannelMixer.

The VoiceIsolation tests now use production-shaped 10 ms buffers
instead of 20 ms ones, and name their stereo input levels.
CreateComponentProcesses10MsFrames checks that CreateComponent()
returns a 10 ms component with 20 ms of algorithmic delay, and
ClearBuffersPurgesStaleLookaheadAudio wraps its STFT in
BufferedVoiceIsolation like the production pipeline.

[Permissions] Guard against null mediator in dismissFromNative

When draining queued permission dialogs without an available
ModalDialogManager (e.g. during tab destruction or window teardown),
PermissionDialogCoordinator.showDialog() synchronously invokes
PermissionDialogDelegate.onDismiss(AUTODISMISS_NO_DIALOG_MANAGER). The
resulting native prompt destruction synchronously calls back into Java
dismissFromNative(). Because mMediator is only initialized when
ModalDialogManager is present, dismissFromNative() dereferenced a null
mMediator via assumeNonNull(), throwing a NullPointerException.

* Check for non-null mMediator before delegating in
  PermissionDialogCoordinator.dismissFromNative().
* Add Robolectric test in PermissionDialogCoordinatorTest verifying
  synchronous dismissFromNative() when ModalDialogManager is null.

parent
67827e6d7bb4886d1ca586a2f50f038d22cf18ea [ diff ] 
media: Add BufferedVoiceIsolation

APM works at 100 Hz, but VoiceIsolation works at 50 Hz to reduce the
computational cost. This change adds BufferedVoiceIsolation, a
VoiceIsolationComponent that buffers two consecutive 10 ms frames and
runs the wrapped component once on the combined 20 ms frame. It adds
one 10 ms frame of algorithmic latency.

The component is not used yet. Follow-up CLs will:
- Wrap the STFT pipeline in BufferedVoiceIsolation inside
  CreateVoiceIsolation().
- Replace the ConvertingAudioFifo instances (forward_fifo_ and
  backward_fifo_) with a ChannelMixer, so VoiceIsolation processes each
  480-frame 48 kHz APM buffer directly. Steady-state latency does not
  change, because the FIFOs already added one 10 ms frame. The resampler
  is no longer needed after https://crrev.com/c/8460146.

AmbientLoginPermissionRequest that are needed for integration with the

[iOS][TTC] Implement TTCWebSocketBackend and wire into TTCConversation

Implements TTCWebSocketBackend conforming to the TTCBackend protocol
to enable bidirectional live audio streaming with a streaming service
over WebSockets via Apple's native NSURLSessionWebSocketTask.

- Establishes connection to the configured WebSocket endpoint with
  api_key authentication and delegates connection events to the
  calling sequence runner.
- Transmits initial session setup frame configuring model, voice
  persona, linear PCM audio modality, and system instructions.
- Implements audio stream backpressure throttling (kMaxInFlightAudioSends)
  to ensure real-time latency under varying network throughput.
- Parses incoming JSON messages from the streaming service, dispatching
  audio output chunks, turn completion, transcriptions, and
  server-side barge-in interruption events to TTCBackendDelegate.
- Sends periodic heartbeat pings to keep intermediate proxy and
  NAT connections alive.
- Wires TTCWebSocketBackend into TTCConversation init.
- Exposes internal testing category in a dedicated testing header
  (ttc_websocket_backend+Testing.h) with class methods for payload
  creation and properties for in-flight audio send tracking.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests covering setup payload creation,
  audio chunk formatting, text turn serialization, message parsing,
  and connection error handling.

Android: Fix NPE in NativePageBitmapCapturer when tab.getView() is null

TabImpl#getView() returns null when a native page is frozen in the
background or when the tab is detached from its activity, even though
TabImpl#isNativePage() remains true and TabImpl#getWindowAndroid() is
non-null.

(and null WebContents in isCapturable), and also ensure
maybeCaptureNativeViewSync verifies view/container readiness via
shouldUseFallbackUx before capturing.

[EdgeToEdge] Keep bottom chin composited while BCIV controls scroll on

Under browser controls in viz (BCIV with OffsetTag), Viz translates the
chin layer using the renderer's offset, while BottomControlsStacker only
dispatches the chin's resting offset to the browser
(BottomControlsStacker.java:521-522). EdgeToEdgeBottomChinMediator
previously bound IS_VISIBLE (which gates
EdgeToEdgeBottomChinSceneLayer's scene overlay tree) to isVisible(),
which relied on the browser's lagging getBottomControlOffset(). When the
renderer scrolls or animates controls back on screen and the offset
crosses below chin height (72px on test device), the chin layer was
dropped from the compositor frame for a frame, exposing the tab
background under the bottom bar.

This CL ensures the chin layer remains composited during BCIV scrolling:
* Introduces isVisibleBasedOnOffset() (mYOffset < HEIGHT) to drive
  IS_VISIBLE at construction, updateHeightAndVisibility(), and
  onBrowserControlsOffsetUpdate(), matching
  ScrollingBottomViewSceneLayer.
* Retains isVisible() strictly to gate color and divider updates so the
  chin preserves the bottom controls color while scrolled off.
* Adds 3 new EdgeToEdgeBottomChinMediatorTest cases (2 fail without fix;
  46/46 pass across Mediator/SceneLayer/Coordinator tests).
* Verified on 1080x1920 emulator with gesture navigation and
  --enable-features=AndroidBottomBar: missing chin frame reproduced in
  5/5 runs before, 0/6 after.

Adjust TabDialogManagerBrowserTest to work on Wayland

TL;DR: This required parenting test dialog widgets to the browser window
in TabDialogManagerBrowserTest like production code does.

In TabDialogManagerBrowserTest, dialog widgets created by
CreateAutoresizeWidget() and CreateWidgetWithNoNonClientView() were
initialized without a parent native window. Consequently, on Linux
with Wayland/Ozone, they were initialized as desktop top-level surfaces
(xdg_toplevel).

On Wayland, client-driven positioning of toplevel surfaces is not
supported (supports_global_screen_coordinates is false), and the
Wayland compositor configures toplevel window origins to (0, 0).
As a result, tests expecting the widget's screen origin to change
(such as ChangePreferredSizeAfterSplitViewCreated) would capture or
remain stuck at origin (0, 0), causing WaitForState() to time out
waiting for bounds repositioning.

This CL updates the test helper functions to accept an optional parent
gfx::NativeView and passes the browser window's native window in the
affected tests. This mirrors how TabDialogManager::CreateTabScopedDialog
parents dialogs in production, ensuring the test widgets are child Aura
windows that can be positioned and moved properly across all platforms
including Wayland.

[iOS] Add TipsNotificationsEphemeralModule for Magic Stack Tips

Implement `TipsNotificationEphemeralModule` to evaluate and rank the
tips notifications tip in the Magic Stack:
- Require `kNotOptInTipsNotifications` and
  `kTipsOptInPromptNotReceivedRecently` signals, and disqualify new
   users (`kIsNewUser`) or users who have already interacted with the
   module.
-Track module impressions and interactions via profile prefs. -Register
  `TipsNotificationEphemeralModule` in `HomeModulesCardRegistryIOS` via
  `AddCardForTip()`, `RegisterProfilePrefs()`, and
  `IsEphemeralTipsModuleLabel()`.

[iOS] Notify TipsManager when a Tips notification opt-in prompt is shown

Notifies `TipsManagerIOS` with the
`kTipsNotificationOptInPromptReceived` signal whenever the user is
prompted to opt into Tips notifications—either via the notifications
opt-in screen (`NotificationsOptInCoordinator`) or the system/settings
permission alert (`NotificationsOptInAlertCoordinator` when `kTips` is
in `clientIds`).
This tracks recent opt-in prompts for the Magic Stack V2 Notifications
tip eligibility check.

Drop and block fullscreen while save/file pickers are open

Browser-initiated file pickers take focus and fire window.blur, allowing
a page with transient user activation to call requestFullscreen() and
cover the picker. Call WebContents::ForSecurityDropFullscreen() while
SavePackageFilePicker, DownloadFilePicker,
BrowserSelectFileDialogController, and DownloadDialogBridge are open.

Disable filling on page load when MarkAllCredentialsAsLeaked is enabled

When MarkAllCredentialsAsLeaked is enabled for testing, credentials
stored in the password store may not have InsecureType::kLeaked in
password_issues. Treat them as leaked in IsEligibleForPasswordChange so
that credentials are not autofilled on page load and automated password
change can be offered.

[Startup] Defer ContextualSearch native and TemplateUrlService

During WebContents initialization for loading tabs,
ContextualSearchTabHelper [1] eagerly instantiated its native C++
helper over JNI, registered observers on TemplateUrlService, and
evaluated search engine state.

Defers ContextualSearchTabHelper native and hook initialization until
ContextualSearch is active (after manager creation) when
ClankStartupTabOptimizations is enabled.

https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:chrome/android/java/src/org/chromium/chrome/browser/contextualsearch/ContextualSearchTabHelper.java;l=196;drc=70aa61b0bffc63cb84c5422b6654391372a04d4b
